events.description: With the release of sensor version 7.11, CrowdStrike introduced the new IPC Template Type, delivered as Rapid Response Content via Channel File 291; its definition expected 21 input fields while the sensor code supplied only 20.

Manual and automated testing of the IPC Template Type was performed; automated tests used a static set of 12 test cases with a wildcard matching criterion in the 21st field, and the stress test passed without triggering a fault.
The first several IPC Template Instances were deployed to production in Rapid Response Content updates; they used wildcard matching criteria for the 21st input and deployed successfully.
Two additional IPC Template Instances were deployed, one introducing a non-wildcard matching criterion for the 21st input, producing a new version of Channel File 291.
The Content Validator evaluated the new Template Instances based on the expectation of 21 inputs and passed them, and they were sent to sensors.

events.time: July 19, 2024 (at next IPC notification after receipt)
events.description: Windows sensors receiving the new Channel File 291 evaluated the Template Instances at the next IPC notification; accessing the 21st input value caused an out-of-bounds memory read and the system crashed with a PAGE_FAULT_IN_NONPAGED_AREA bugcheck in csagent.sys.
Recovery status: using week-over-week comparison, approximately 99% of Windows sensors were online compared to before the content update (typical variance ~1%).
